headings.title: SMTO-EXE-0065 — SMTO can't tell if its change on the Gateway computer happened

html:
SMTO-EXE-0065 — SMTO can't tell if its change on the Gateway computer happened

GUID: eb906162-8ab6-5623-b11f-f3dce9683865
Slug: desktop-outcome-unknown
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: desktop

What happened

  • SMTO tried to open, close, quit or move something on the Gateway computer, but lost the answer before it could confirm the result. The change may or may not have happened.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look at the Gateway computer's screen, or ask SMTO to list the open apps and windows there. Don't ask it to change anything yet. SMTO couldn't confirm the result, so the app may already be open, closed or moved.
  2. If SMTO can't reach that computer, open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection for that Gateway, then look again. SMTO can only check what happened through the same Gateway that received the request.
  3. Only if the change clearly did not happen, ask SMTO to do it once more. Repeating an open or quit that already worked can start a second copy of an app or close one you need.

What success looks like

  • You've confirmed the app or window is in the state you wanted, and the action ran only once.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with what you saw on the screen, to the person who manages the Gateway computer. Don't keep repeating the open, close, quit or end-program request while the result is unclear.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Desktop change (launch, activate, close, quit, terminate or window move/state) lost its reliable result or reported uncertain effects, and the single follow-up observation on the same Gateway could not prove the requested state.

What this means

  • An attempted desktop mutation lost a reliable result, native action reported uncertain effects or the existing reconciliation checks could not confirm the requested state. These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.

Why this can happen

  • An attempted desktop mutation lost a reliable result, native action reported uncertain effects or the existing reconciliation checks could not confirm the requested state.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original action and current exact process/window identity; distinguish a lost acknowledgment from a proven unsuccessful action.

How to fix it

  • Reconnect the same Gateway and observe the target (process_info with the original pid and process_identity, applications, or windows with the window_id) to settle the original operation, and check the Gateway log for the original execution_id. Do not repeat launch, close, quit or terminate until that observation shows it did not take effect.
  • Reconnect the same Gateway and inspect current processes or windows. Do not repeat a launch, close, quit or signal without reconciling its effects.

Retry and execution caution

  • Reconnect the same Gateway and inspect current processes or windows. Do not repeat a launch, close, quit or signal without reconciling its effects.

How to verify the fix

  • The original launch, close, quit, signal or window change is reconciled before any repeat.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass identity protection or automatically replay an uncertain mutation.

Technical notes

  • These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
